Ad programming

Loading

Removes recognized advertising fields from startup responses. All video data passes through. Unknown responses stay unchanged. This setting affects new requests; it does not end an ad already playing.

Allowed video

Loading

While the filter is active, other identifiers and unidentified media are withheld on the Mac. Another video may be an ad or a preload: its ID alone cannot decide. Content already cached on the iPhone remains playable. Ads confirmed in responses remain listed after Clear; this does not prove they were displayed.

What is blocked or allowed

Blocked in filtering mode

    These domains and all their subdomains. They also pass through in observation mode.

    Connections established; media subject to the filter above

    • *.googlevideo.com
    • *.youtube.com
    • youtubei.googleapis.com
    • youtube.googleapis.com
    • *.ytimg.com · yt3.ggpht.com

    Googlevideo connections stay open so identifiers can be read; this does not mean all media is forwarded. Other public HTTPS destinations on port 443 also pass unless they are on the blocklist.

    What these numbers mean

    Blocked = this connection was rejected. No server content passes through that attempt. This does not prove an ad disappeared: it may already be cached or arrive through another request.

    A connection is not an advertisement. A tunnel can carry several requests; retries are counted separately.

    Paths on googlevideo.com become visible in observe-media mode. Their name alone does not prove a stream is an ad.

    For new tunnels, “Flow details” shows the contacted IP, byte counts, and receive times. Identifiers and withheld bytes appear in the HTTPS tables above.

    The log shows YouTube and advertising families recorded by the proxy. Other domains, full URLs, and traffic bypassing the proxy are not visible here.
